introduce:
Start with your knees and hands on the floor. Put your hands a little forward, widen your knees and put your toes together. 

Take a breath, then exhale and sit back. Try to make your butt touch your heels. Relax your elbows, make your forehead touch the floor and try to lower your chest close to the floor. Hold this position.

Keep your arms stretched forward as you sit back. Make sure there is enough space between your shoulders and ears during the exercise.
name: CHILD'S POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please make sure there is enough space between your shoulders and ears.
Please keep your arms stretched forward as you sit back.
This exercise gently stretches your upper back, shoulders, hips and legs.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Raise your arms at your sides to shoulder height with your palms down.

Turn your left foot to the left and your right foot 45 degrees to the left. Slightly shift your hips to the right, and bend your torso to the left until your left hand presses on the floor. 

Extend your right arm toward the ceiling, and turn your head to look at your right hand. Hold this position.
name: TRIANGLE POSE LEFT

tips.text: Please keep your chest facing forward.
Please keep your arms and legs straight during the exercise.
If you feel it\'s too hard, put your left hand on your left leg instead of the floor.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Raise your arms at your sides to shoulder height with your palms down. 

Turn your right foot to the right and your left foot 45 degrees to the right. Slightly shift your hips to the left, and bend your torso to the right until your right hand presses on the floor. 

Extend your left arm toward the ceiling, and turn your head to look at your left hand. Hold this position.
name: TRIANGLE POSE RIGHT

tips.text: Please keep your chest facing forward.
Please keep your arms and legs straight during the exercise.
If you feel it\'s too hard, put your right hand on your right leg instead of the floor.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Lie on your back with your arms on your sides. Lift your legs up. Slightly tuck your chin towards your chest. \n\nAs you exhale, use your abdominal strength to roll your legs back until they are parallel to the ground, then inhale and lower your back on the ground. Repeat the exercise.
name: PILATES ROLL OVER

tips.text: Please do it on a mat.
You shouldn’t feel pressure on your neck.
Please do it slowly to avoid injuries.
Exhale as you roll back, and inhale as you come back.

introduce:
Stand with feet a little wider than shoulder width apart. 

Raise your hands overhead with palms up toward the ceiling. 

Use one of your hands to grab the other. Bend your body side to side.
name: STANDING BACK STRETCHES

tips.text: Inhale when you bend down, and exhale when you come back.
This exercise helps stretch your spine.

introduce:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and shift your weight onto your right leg. 

Then bend and lift your left knee, and draw your left heel against your right inner thigh. Place your hands in front of your chest in a praying position. 

Hold this position.
name: TREE POSE RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep looking ahead.
Extend your spine.
Press your foot against your inner thigh.
Don\'t press your foot on knee joint of standing leg.
Engage your abs to maintain balance instead of ankle.
Breathe slowly and evenly.
If too easy for you, extend your arms overhead, and keep your elbows straight.
If too hard for you, lower heel to your calf or ankle.
Your neck and shoulders should not feel tense.
This is a good exercise for your core and your lower body.

introduce:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and shift your weight onto your left leg. 

Then bend and lift your right knee, and draw your right heel against your left inner thigh. Place your hands in front of your chest in a praying position. 

Hold this position.
name: TREE POSE LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep looking ahead.
Extend your spine.
Press your foot against your inner thigh.
Don\'t press your foot on knee joint of standing leg.
Engage your abs to maintain balance instead of ankle.
Breathe slowly and evenly.
If too easy for you, extend your arms overhead, and keep your elbows straight.
If too hard for you, lower heel to your calf or ankle.
Your neck and shoulders should not feel tense.
This is a good exercise for your core and your lower body.

introduce:
Lie on your back with your legs lifted, and your legs and buttocks against the wall. 

Pull your toes toward your body, then stretch your ankles and try to use your toes to touch the wall. Repeat the exercise.

Breathe naturally. This exercise stretches your calves and hamstrings.
name: STRETCH LEGS ON THE WALL

tips.text: Please find a wall.
Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your legs straight.
Please keep your lower back always on the floor.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise stretches your calves and hamstrings.

introduce: Sit on the floor with your feet hip width apart. Lift your arms at shoulder height, curl your chin towards your chest. Reach your hands forward to touch your toes, then return and repeat.\n\nExhale as you reach forward, and inhale as you return. This exercise stretches your calves, hamstrings and back.
name: FORWARD SPINE STRETCH PULSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Exhale as you reach forward, and inhale as you return.
Pull your toes toward your body.
Bring your shoulders down away from your ears.
This exercise stretches your calves, hamstrings and back.

introduce: Lie on your stomach with your legs extended and your arms by your sides. \n\nLift your shoulders, legs, and arms off the floor with your palms towards the ceiling. Hold this position.
name: LOCUST POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your pelvis on the floor when lifting your legs.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise tones your buttocks and strengthens your back muscles.

introduce:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart. Draw your belly in and tuck your tailbone down. Roll your shoulders back and down. 

Bend your upper body forward and rest your hands on your legs. Bend from your hips instead of your waist. 

Focus on keeping your back flat and lengthening your spine. Hold this position.
name: HALF FORWARD BEND

tips.text: Bend from your hips instead of your waist.
Keep your legs straight but don\'t lock your knees.
Focus on keeping your back flat and lengthening your spine.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise stretches your hamstrings.
This exercise strengthens your back.

introduce:
Stand upright with your arms by your sides. Interlock your fingers and turn your palms upwards. 

Inhale, stretch your arms to the ceiling while simultaneously raising your heels. Your balance will shift to your toes. 

Hold for seconds. Return and repeat.
name: PALM TREE POSE

tips.text: Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Keep your back straight.
This exercise stretches your entire body and improves your balance.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Start on all fours with your hips up in an upside-down \'V\' shape. Alternately lift and lower your heels.
name: WALK THE DOG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Relax your neck.
Breathe regularly.
Notice the elongation from your fingertips to your sit bone.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Please press all areas of the palms equally on the floor.
This exercise stretches your shoulders, hamstrings, calves, and arches.

introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart. 

Turn your left foot to the left and your right foot 60 degrees to the left.

Bend your left leg until your thigh is almost parallel to the floor. 

Bend your upper body to the left and rest your left elbow on your left knee.

Extend your right arm by your ear to the left. Hold this position.
name: EXTENDED SIDE ANGLE LEFT

tips.text: Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Don\'t let your knee go over your toes.
Keep your knees in line with your toes.
Put your weight mainly on your legs instead of your elbow.
This exercise strengthens your shoulders, thighs, and glutes.
This exercise stretches your groins, hamstrings, waist, and shoulders.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart. 

Turn your right foot to the right and your left foot 60 degrees to the right.

Bend your right leg until your thigh is almost parallel to the floor. 

Bend your upper body to the right and rest your right elbow on your right knee.

Extend your left arm by your ear to the right. Hold this position.
name: EXTENDED SIDE ANGLE RIGHT

tips.text: Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Don't let your knee go over your toes.
Keep your knees in line with your toes.
Put your weight mainly on your legs instead of your elbow.
This exercise strengthens your shoulders, thighs, and glutes.
This exercise stretches your groins, hamstrings, waist, and shoulders.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Lie down on your stomach and bend your elbows with your hands beneath your shoulders.

Keep your toes back and your feet and legs relaxed on the ground.

Then push your chest up off the ground as far as possible. Return to the start position and repeat.
name: COBRAS

tips.text: Prepare a mat first.
Tighten your abdominals.
Stretch your abdominals as much as you can.
Inhale when you go up, and exhale when you go down.
This is a great exercise to strengthen your back.
